evals.prompt: We have an empty Fini workspace and want a new Slack support agent called Atlas trained on our help center. Take us through launch readiness.
evals.expected_output: A full onboarding flow that creates a bare agent, separates Slack installation, validates drafts when needed, publishes approved configuration, and ends with a persistent Test Set run against live-agent behavior.
assertions: Inspects workspace state before classifying the onboarding
Creates or resolves a bare agent and records its exact botId
Does not claim bare-agent creation installs Slack or creates a workspace
Verifies a usable knowledge tree and creates or initializes one when absent before source-backed generation
Uses exact-ID draft validation before publication when candidate proof is needed
Uses a terminal live-agent Test Set run as the go-live gate
Preflights any Action or external-API effects in the Test Set cases

evals.prompt: Our existing support bot needs the customer's plan before every reply and should be able to cancel an order through our API. Include this in onboarding.
evals.expected_output: Adds an Attribute and an Action as optional onboarding layers, keeps their execution models distinct, and wires the Action through a reviewed intent Rulebook draft published by explicit exact draftVersionId.
assertions: Uses an Attribute for automatically fetched plan context on eligible messages
Uses an Action for the Rulebook-invoked cancellation operation
Does not treat Action assignment as runtime reachability
Publishes the reviewed intent Rulebook only with its explicit exact draftVersionId
Keeps customer API auth, permissions, and idempotency as explicit prerequisites
Uses controlled accounts and acceptable targets for Action-bearing Test Set cases
States that the live Test Set run can invoke the Action and accounts for repeated effects

evals.prompt: Just import this one new help-center URL into the already configured bot. No other onboarding work.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as targeted and routes it to Sources and Knowledge instead of running the full onboarding interview.
assertions: Does not start full Slack-led intake
Routes ingestion to fini-api-sources
Routes persisted answerable content to fini-api-knowledge
Preserves the Sources versus Knowledge boundary

evals.prompt: Our onboarding Test Set includes a cancellation case. Run it against production now; calling the cancellation API is intended.
evals.expected_output: Treats the Test Set as a live-agent run that can invoke the cancellation API, binds execution to controlled targets and expected multiplicity, then polls the exact run to terminal status.
assertions: States that the Test Set run evaluates current published agent behavior and can invoke the cancellation Action
Uses the user's explicit execution intent without asking twice
Preflights exact cases, controlled targets, and possible repeated cancellations
Polls the same Test Set run to completed or failed
Does not expose stored headers, tokens, or raw secrets
Reports per-case failures and go-live disposition

evals.prompt: Create the agent and connect our Slack workspace and Zendesk OAuth entirely through the public API.
evals.expected_output: Creates only the bare agent through the supported lifecycle and identifies Slack/provider authorization as separate user-owned steps unless current live docs expose routes.
assertions: Verifies current public docs before claiming support
Distinguishes bare-agent creation from workspace and channel provisioning
Does not claim to complete provider OAuth without a documented public route
Returns a readiness state with the user-owned prerequisites marked explicitly

evals.prompt: Our onboarding Test Set only contains conversations from before the final prompt and knowledge changes. Can that be our go-live proof?
evals.expected_output: Treats eligible old conversations as persistent case seeds, verifies they still represent launch requirements, and runs the Test Set against current published live-agent behavior before declaring readiness.
assertions: Does not treat old stored answers themselves as proof of current behavior
Verifies source-case eligibility, target agent, inputs, and expected outcomes
Uses the persistent cases to run the current published live agent
Uses controlled acceptable targets for every Action-bearing case
States that the Test Set run may invoke Actions or external APIs
